title: A frozen 1950-2002 spring temperature and winter precipitation model predicted 2003-2025 snowmelt runoff timing at 60 western US reference gauges within 1 day; 8 Washington gauges ran 8 days early
abstract: Stewart, Cayan and Dettinger (2005) related earlier western North American snowmelt runoff in 1948-2002 mainly to warmer springs. We tested this explanation out of sample. We used 60 snowmelt-dominated CAMELS-US reference gauges west of 103 W and USGS daily discharge. In each gauge we fitted the center of timing (CT, flow-weighted mean day of the water year) to basin-mean March-May temperature and log October-March precipitation (NOAA nClimGrid) for 1950-2002. We froze the models and predicted 2003-2025 from observed climate. We wrote the plan and a null criterion (|bias| < 3 days) before we calculated CT. The pooled mean residual was -0.85 days (95% interval -2.36 to +0.64 by year bootstrap; -3.67 to +1.96 by region-year bootstrap). The model reduced the test mean squared error by 37% against climatology and by 31% against an extrapolated trend. Mean CT was 4.67 days earlier in 2003-2025; the frozen temperature terms give -4.30 days, precipitation +0.45 days, and -0.82 days are not explained. Five pre-registered variants (other temperature windows, no precipitation term, Q25 and Q50 dates) gave residuals of -1.07 to +0.68 days. Exploratory: 8 Washington Cascade and Olympic gauges ran 7.99 days earlier than predicted (-12.2 to -4.0), while the other 52 gauges gave +0.25 days (-1.48 to +1.81). RGI 7.0 glacier cover did not order this residual (the glacier-free American River was 8.8 days early). Higher October-December flow gives about 40% of it, and smaller June-September shares most of the rest; separate autumn precipitation terms remove about one quarter. The pooled temperature slope was -5.07 days per C in 1950-2002 and -6.91 in 2003-2025 (difference interval -3.52 to +0.03). Limitations: only 60 small reference basins, interpolated mountain climate, a linear two-predictor model without snowpack data, a post hoc Washington subgroup that needs an independent test, glacier centroids instead of outlines, and some provisional 2024-2025 flow values.

display.caption: Mean CT anomaly of 60 western US snowmelt gauges: observed (blue) and per-gauge temperature + precipitation model fitted to 1950-2002 (orange), frozen in the shaded 2003-2025 test period.
Mean 2003-2025 CT residual at each gauge (red = earlier than the frozen model). Rings mark |z| > 2. The early cluster is in the Washington Cascades and Olympics.

A: Season contributions to the mean CT residual for 8 Washington Cascade/Olympic gauges and 52 other gauges. B: CT residual against RGI 7.0 glacier cover; glacier cover does not order the Washington signal.
